title: Delivery workers rally against New York City labor bill
seoTitle: NYC delivery workers rally against labor bill

tea.why: Delivery workers and employers protested against the mayor-backed Delivery Protection Act.
tea.want: They demanded that City Hall meet with them and reconsider the legislation that could impact their jobs.
tea.changed: Oct 22: Delivery workers and employers held a rally outside City Hall to voice concerns over the Delivery Protection Act.

summary: Delivery workers and employers gathered near City Hall in New York City on Thursday to protest the mayor-backed Delivery Protection Act. Organised groups including the New York Delivers Coalition warned that the legislation threatens thousands of jobs and could close small delivery businesses by banning Amazon from utilizing third-party contractors. Protesters voiced concerns about job security and livelihoods, calling for discussions among stakeholders. Meanwhile, supporters of the bill, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani, City Council Member Tiffany Cabán, and the Teamsters, defended the legislation on the steps of City Hall, arguing it ensures accountability and protects workers from exploitation. Amazon stated that the claims were flawed and noted it would consider leaving the city if the bill passed.
demands: Meet with City Hall officials regarding the legislation
response: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and City Council Member Tiffany Cabán defended the bill at a counter-rally, arguing it holds companies accountable. Amazon stated the exploitation claim was flawed and warned it could consider leaving the city if the legislation passes.

updates.text: Delivery workers and business owners rallied outside City Hall on Thursday to protest the Delivery Protection Act.
